On a candidate T=(ps+j)b+zc, 0<=j<s and 0<=z<u, reduction mod u forces any representation's c-count Z=z+ut and the size bound forces t∈{0,1}. The t=0 equations have p+1 solutions at T, p after subtracting any positive k<=s copies of a; the t=1 branch contributes exactly one extra solution when j=s-1 and k<=h, yielding the single exceptional row subtraction ha. The a=us residues are all represented exactly once; monotonicity of denumerants upon adding a proves minimality. Summing Apéry elements gives n_p, and max-a gives g_p.
